name: R&S Records
blurb: Renaat Vandepapeliere's house started in Belgian new beat, then opened the door for everyone who mattered between Detroit and Sheffield: Beltram, Aphex on Apollo, Sun Electric, the whole Ferox lineage. Jet-yellow sleeves. Run by feel.

name: Apollo
blurb: R&S sublabel for ambient. Selected Ambient Works Vol. II lives here. Quiet weight.

name: Warp Records
blurb: Steve Beckett and Rob Mitchell's Sheffield record shop became the most influential electronic label of the 90s. Bleep techno first, then IDM, then everything that didn't fit. Aphex, Autechre, Boards of Canada, Squarepusher. Designs Republic on the sleeves.

name: Tresor
blurb: Berlin techno temple. Started as a bunker club, then the label that Detroit and Berlin met inside. Jeff Mills, Joey Beltram, Cristian Vogel, Surgeon, plus the X-103 / X-102 conceptual records that made techno feel like science fiction.

name: Trax Records
blurb: Larry Sherman's Chicago house origin label. Frankie Knuckles, Marshall Jefferson, Ron Hardy, Adonis. The records that named the genre, even if the artists barely got paid for them.

name: DJ International Records
blurb: Rocky Jones' Chicago house imprint. Ran parallel to Trax, equally foundational. Steve "Silk" Hurley, Farley "Jackmaster" Funk, Tyree Cooper. Released the first 12"s the rest of the world bought as "house".

name: Dance Mania
blurb: The Chicago label that mutated house into ghetto-house. Ray Barney's imprint. DJ Funk, DJ Deeon, DJ Milton, Paul Johnson. Trunk-rattling 808 minimalism that the internet would later steal wholesale.

name: Strictly Rhythm
blurb: Mark Finkelstein's NYC garage/house empire. Armand Van Helden, Roger Sanchez, Erick Morillo, Kerri Chandler. Hundreds of 12"s, most of them hits in clubrooms before they were anywhere else.

name: Nervous Records
blurb: Michael Weiss's NYC label. Masters At Work, Kerri Chandler, MAW productions. Garage, house, the deep-house tradition continued.

name: Nu Groove Records
blurb: Frank and Karen Mendez's NYC label. Burrell Brothers, Bobby Konders, Joey Beltram's earliest 12"s. Four years, hundreds of records, no compromise.

name: Underground Resistance
blurb: Mike Banks and Jeff Mills' Detroit techno militancy. Sleeves stamped with manifestos. Distribution via Submerge. "Riot", "Final Frontier", "The Theory". The X-101/102/103 conceptual trilogy.

name: Transmat
blurb: Derrick May's label. Strings of Life, Beyond the Dance, the Innovator compilation. The bridge between Chicago house and what would become techno.

name: Metroplex
blurb: Juan Atkins' label, the founding document of Detroit techno. Cybotron and Model 500 records that imagined a Black electronic future.

name: KMS Records
blurb: Kevin Saunderson's label. Inner City, Reese Project, the rolling house-techno hybrid that broke into UK pop charts.

name: Plus 8 Records
blurb: Richie Hawtin and John Acquaviva's Windsor-Detroit imprint. Plastikman lives here. Acid, minimalism, the records that made Berlin's nineties possible.

name: M-Plant
blurb: Robert Hood's label. Minimal techno reduced to its essential frequency. Sleeves in monochrome, tracks in monochrome.

name: Axis Records
blurb: Jeff Mills' label. The Bells, Waveform Transmission. Three-deck mixes pressed to wax.

name: Planet E Communications
blurb: Carl Craig's label. Detroit jazz-techno, Innerzone Orchestra, the Designer Music compilations.

name: 430 West
blurb: Octave One's label. Detroit techno that ran on rhythm rather than concept.

name: Junior Boy's Own
blurb: Steven Hall and Terry Farley's London imprint. Underworld, Chemical Brothers' debut, the records that turned UK house into something more like pop. Sleeves like football fanzines.

name: Soma Quality Recordings
blurb: Slam's Glasgow techno label. Daft Punk's first records came out here as much as anywhere. Funk d'Void, Envoy, the Slam productions themselves.

name: Ovum Recordings
blurb: Josh Wink's label. Higher State of Consciousness, Quadrasync, US house with a tougher European pulse.

name: Mute
blurb: Daniel Miller's UK electronic establishment. Depeche Mode pays for the experimental subsidiaries; Throbbing Gristle, Cabaret Voltaire, Boyd Rice live in the back rooms.

name: NovaMute
blurb: Mute's techno sublabel. Plastikman, Speedy J, Luke Slater, Beltram's mid-period. The Mute approach with a 909 attached.

name: Mille Plateaux
blurb: Achim Szepanski's Frankfurt IDM/glitch label. Named after Deleuze and Guattari. Oval, Pole, Alec Empire's quieter work, the Clicks & Cuts compilations.

name: Force Inc. Music Works
blurb: Frankfurt techno parent of Mille Plateaux. Acid, hardcore, abstract techno. Achim Szepanski again.

name: Ninja Tune
blurb: Coldcut's label. Trip-hop, leftfield breaks, beats. Amon Tobin, Funki Porcini, DJ Vadim, Mr. Scruff.

name: Mo Wax
blurb: James Lavelle's leftfield/trip-hop label. UNKLE, DJ Krush, the Headz compilations. Futura 2000 sleeves.

name: Basic Channel
blurb: Moritz von Oswald and Mark Ernestus' Berlin dub-techno foundation. Numbered, plain-sleeve 12"s. Hard Wax distributes.

name: Chain Reaction
blurb: Basic Channel sublabel. Porter Ricks, Monolake, Vainqueur. Dub techno that explored the harmonics rather than the chords.

name: Rhythm & Sound
blurb: Basic Channel's Jamaican project. Tikiman, the version mixes, dub techno that finally remembered it was dub.

name: Maurizio
blurb: Basic Channel side-project. Numbered series. Few words spoken.

name: Kompakt
blurb: Wolfgang Voigt's Cologne minimal/microhouse label. Total compilations, the Pop Ambient series, Michael Mayer, Superpitcher, DJ Koze.

name: Profan
blurb: Wolfgang Voigt's earlier Cologne imprint. Where the Kompakt sound began.

name: Perlon
blurb: Markus Nikolai's Berlin minimal label. Ricardo Villalobos, Zip, Sammy Dee. Tracks that go for fifteen minutes and don't apologise.

name: DJAX-Up-Beats
blurb: Saskia Slegers' Dutch acid-techno label. Mike Dearborn, Acid Junkies, K. Hand. Made acid sound European.

name: Music Man Records
blurb: Belgian techno foundation, run by R&S alum. CJ Bolland, Frank de Wulf. Tougher and more European than its R&S sibling.

name: Hard Wax
blurb: Berlin record shop and distribution-tied imprint. Basic Channel, Chain Reaction, Maurizio all flow through here. The shop is the curation.

name: Sähkö Recordings
blurb: Finnish minimal techno. Mika Vainio (Pan Sonic), Jimi Tenor's earlier work. White sleeves, sine waves.

name: XL Recordings
blurb: Started as a UK hardcore/breakbeat label. SL2's "On a Ragga Tip", The Prodigy's first three albums. Eventually became a major in everything but ownership.

name: Reinforced Records
blurb: 4hero's UK hardcore label that became the cradle of drum & bass. Goldie's debut, Doc Scott, Nookie. The records where breakbeat learned to swing.

name: Moving Shadow
blurb: Rob Playford's UK breakbeat / d&b label. Foul Play, Omni Trio, the Moving Shadow series compilations.
